title: Why Your Company Needs a Context Graph (and How to Build It) — Gil Feig, Merge
talk_summary: Gil Feig argues that MCP live lookups alone can't answer semantic/aggregate questions because third-party APIs don't support them, so you need a synced local copy plus a router/summarizer and a skills/memory layer to select and compress context. He also stresses storing provenance metadata (source, fetch time, scope, invalidation rules) on every piece of context.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of live MCP lookups for questions spanning large datasets, they sync a local copy (vector DB) and pre-store derived summaries so repeated/common questions don't re-fetch and re-summarize.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you need any form of semantic look ups... you have to sync a copy

takeaways.what_they_do: A router decides which handler gets the prompt; a summarizer compresses aggregated synced+live context before returning it to the calling agent, avoiding dumping massive retrieved context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can't just dump a massive amount of retrieved context back to our agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Company-specific definitions (e.g., 'what does customer-happy mean') live as skills checked first; only then does the agent decide which data sources to hit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your agent should first check the skills before it then goes and starts checking your synced layer

takeaways.what_they_do: Every synced/derived context stores source, fetch time, ID/scope, permissions, transform history, and an invalidation rule (e.g., age > 1 month).
takeaways.evidence_quote: Where did we fetch it? When did we fetch it?... what should invalidate it?

takeaways.technique: Prefer live lookups, cache only when needed
takeaways.what_they_do: Simple single-record lookups stay as live MCP calls (cheaper, simpler); only semantic/aggregate needs get the heavier synced cache.
